clue.text: Monitored group of swimmers infested by parasites

indicators.note: a group infested by parasites has them right in its midst, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a pod is a group of whales or dolphins
lice are parasitic insects

explanation.surface: A school of dolphins turns out to be crawling with parasites.
explanation.definitionFit: To police something is to keep watch over it and enforce order, so policed is a past-tense synonym of monitored.

clue.text: Maybe hook bearing a pot

indicators.note: bearing means carrying the letter within it

parts.note: a hook is one kind of punch in boxing, hence maybe

explanation.surface: A kitchen hook holding up a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' is a belly here, not a cooking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot or potbelly is a large protruding stomach, which is what a paunch is.

clue.text: Swimmer blocked by fool getting raised pulse, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the letters are read upwards, bottom to top
a word blocked by another has it stuck in its middle

parts.note: an eel is a swimming fish
a mug is a fool or dupe

explanation.surface: A swimmer stopped by a stupid person gets their pulse rate up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' is a heartbeat in the surface, but here a pea or lentil.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses such as lentils and beans are edible seeds of leguminous plants, so a pulse is one example.

clue.text: Awkward to handle cucumber, so messy sandwiches

indicators.note: sandwiches means these words hold the answer between them, contained in their letters

explanation.surface: Cucumber sandwiches are fiddly to eat because they get so messy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumbersome means unwieldy and clumsy, hard to carry or manage.

clue.text: Bird switching ends in park to get such cover

indicators.note: the two ends of park are P and K, and the bird's K is switched for P

parts.note: a drake is a male duck

explanation.surface: A duck in the park changes its ends to get under cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A drape is a curtain or piece of cloth hung as a covering.

clue.text: Recalled what dissecting knife cut: brains

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the whole construction runs in the other direction
something dissecting another cuts into its middle, so it sits inside
a cut word loses its tail, here the last letter of the knife

parts.note: a dagger is a short knife
eh? is a way of saying what? when you have not heard

explanation.surface: Someone remembers what the scalpel sliced through in the lab: the brains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what' is the exclamation eh?, said when you mishear. 'brains' looks like the organ the knife cut, but it means a clever person.
explanation.definitionFit: Brains is informal for a clever person, and an egghead is a bookish intellectual.

clue.text: Bishop's served up drink in church with old friend

indicators.note: in a down clue served up means the letters are read from bottom to top
in places the drink inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a sip is a small drink
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A bishop offers a drink in church with an old friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Episcopal means relating to bishops, from the Greek for overseer, so it matches the possessive.

clue.text: It's surprising how some people request peace

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an exclamation of surprise
second meaning: read as ...! a way of telling someone to be off and keep quiet

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the word into GO and SH, the hush noise, a demand for peace and quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Gosh is a mild exclamation of astonishment, a euphemism for God.

clue.text: Real alien restricting figures going in opposing directions

indicators.note: restricting means holding in, so the figures go inside the alien

parts.note: ET is the alien of the Spielberg film
the figures six and ten, one read backwards and the other forwards, so they run in opposite directions

explanation.surface: An alien holding back numbers that head in opposite directions is real.
explanation.walkthrough: The two figures are six and ten; six is the one written backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Existent means actually existing, which is what real means.

clue.text: Wary detective hidden, joining both Europeans

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

indicators.note: the word has two Europeans; moving one next to the other joins them

parts.note: secret means hidden
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A cautious detective kept out of sight while two Europeans joined him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joining both Europeans' means moving one E of the hidden word so the two sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Discreet means careful and circumspect about what one says, a synonym of wary.

clue.text: A Parisian sad, leaving middle of charlotte free from jam

parts.note: un is French for a, as a Parisian would say it

indicators.note: the named letter is leaving the word, so it is taken out

parts.note: glum means sad

indicators.note: the centre letter of a nine-letter word is its fifth

parts.note: the word charlotte, whose central letter is wanted

explanation.surface: A gloomy French pastry-eater whose charlotte dessert has no jam in it.
explanation.walkthrough: A charlotte is a fruit pudding, which makes 'jam' look culinary; here jam means something stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: To ungum is to unstick, freeing something that was gummed or jammed fast.

clue.text: Servants pushing back minute joints in centre of boat

indicators.note: the minute is pushed back from the front of the word, moving one place later

parts.note: maids are household servants
hips are joints of the body

explanation.surface: Domestic staff hold back a minute while sorting out joints, as on a ship's galley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pushing back' shifts the M of MAIDS one place along, giving AMIDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Amidships is the nautical term for the middle part of a vessel, halfway between bow and stern.

clue.text: Battle formerly with no love for fitness

parts.note: to compete is to battle for something

indicators.note: with no love means the zero letter is removed from the word

parts.note: once means formerly, at an earlier time
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A fight that used to be romantic has lost its love and become about fitness.
explanation.definitionFit: Competence and fitness both mean being suitable or able enough for a task.

clue.text: Luminary talks backwards

indicators.note: backwards means the letters are read from the end to the start

parts.note: to rat is to inform or talk to the authorities, so rats means talks

explanation.surface: A celebrity who speaks in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A luminary is a prominent, famous person, the same idea as a celebrity.

clue.text: Clumsy samurai with the wound

indicators.note: wound is read as wound up, twisted round, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A bungling samurai ends up injuring himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' looks like an injury, but it is the past of wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateurish work is unskilful and inept, lacking professional polish.

clue.text: A limit restricting small cat with energy drink

indicators.note: restricting means holding the other letters in, so they go inside

parts.note: a stint is a limit or restriction, as in without stint
a puma is a large wild cat
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A strict limit keeps a little cat from its energy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A stint as a limit survives in the phrase without stint, meaning without restriction.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti spumante is a sweet sparkling Italian white wine from Piedmont.

clue.text: Spark from one new barrier after it's lifted

indicators.note: after places the barrier word at the end, behind what comes before

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means read upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: the letters of it's, without the apostrophe
a gate is a barrier

explanation.surface: A new barrier is raised, sparking trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To spark a fight is to provoke or start it, which is what instigate means.

clue.text: Swaggered around, supported by props

definitions.meaning: first meaning: walked about in a proud, swaggering way

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning treats the word as a verb from struts, the props used to brace a structure.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both walking with a pompous gait and being braced with supporting struts.

clue.text: Eccentric urged to interrupt boring toil

indicators.note: to interrupt means to break into the middle of a word

parts.note: dry means dull or boring

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre and odd, so the letters go askew

explanation.surface: An oddball urged someone to break off from tedious work.
explanation.definitionFit: Drudgery is hard, menial and monotonous work, which is toil.

clue.text: Ace curried mixture in pastry combined with a fish dish

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the pastry word

parts.note: a tart is a pastry case with filling
A is the card abbreviation for ace
masala is a mixture of ground spices used in curries

explanation.surface: A top-notch spicy filling baked in a tart alongside some seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: Taramasalata is a Greek dip made from fish roe, so it counts as a fish dish.

clue.text: Spells 'discombobulates' as that sounds

indicators.note: as that sounds says the word is said out loud, giving a different spelling

parts.note: fazes means disconcerts or discombobulates

explanation.surface: Someone spells out a word that confuses because of how it sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spells' looks like a verb about writing letters; it is the noun, periods of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell and a phase are both periods or stages, like a dry spell.

clue.text: Becoming fellow who is a member of university staff?

parts.note: a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A man becomes a fellow, which makes him one of the college staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fellow' suggests a college fellow, but becoming means attractive; the wordplay reads 'a don is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis was the beautiful youth of Greek myth, so his name means a handsome young man.

clue.text: Reverse defeat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to cancel or reverse an action
second meaning: to bring about someone's ruin or downfall

explanation.walkthrough: Reads like a description of a sporting comeback, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both cancel an action and, more archaically, ruin or overthrow a person.

clue.text: Drunk duo might be talkative

indicators.note: drunk letters stagger out of order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pair of tipsy people could be rather chatty.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bigmouthed talks too much and indiscreetly, so they are talkative to a fault.

clue.text: Earthwork's annual check's shown missing stone

indicators.note: missing means the named letters are absent from the word

parts.note: an MOT test is the yearly roadworthiness check on British cars
st is the abbreviation for stone, the weight

explanation.surface: An earthwork's yearly inspection shows a stone has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, cars over three years old need an MOT test every year.
explanation.definitionFit: A motte is the mound of earth in a Norman motte-and-bailey castle.

clue.text: Pass beam over front of sailing vessel

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a can is a vessel for holding liquid

explanation.surface: A lighthouse beam sweeps across the bow of a sailing ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan is to sweep a beam such as radar or light across something to examine it.

clue.text: No-nonsense tutor discontented by charm

indicators.note: discontented is read as having its contents taken out, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: to enchant is to charm

explanation.surface: A blunt teacher is unhappy at being won over by charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discontented' looks like unhappiness, but it empties the word tutor, leaving TR.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant comments are incisive and forthright, which is a no-nonsense style.

clue.text: One who made drama of medical condition, case of exaggeration

parts.note: IBS is irritable bowel syndrome, a medical condition

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A hypochondriac makes a drama out of a minor ailment, overstating things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made drama' sounds like fuss; it means writing plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian playwright of A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler.

clue.text: Authority conned to accept foreigner's cash

indicators.note: accepting the cash means taking it in, so it goes inside

parts.note: done means cheated or conned, as in I've been done
the yen is the currency of Japan

explanation.surface: An expert was swindled into taking a bribe in foreign money.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyenne is the most respected woman in a field, an acknowledged expert on it.

clue.text: City penthouses problematic with rent not dropping

indicators.note: rent means torn apart, and problematic penthouses are in a mess, so the letters are rearranged
dropping says the letters of the named word fall out of the mix

parts.note: the word penthouses, taken as written
the word not, whose letters are taken out

explanation.surface: Penthouses in a city become a headache when rent keeps going up.
explanation.walkthrough: Take N, O and T out of PENTHOUSES and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephesus was an ancient Greek city on the coast of Asia Minor, now in Turkey.
